Hess's law

Words: 1k Articles: 3
Thermochemistry OurBigBook.com
Hess's law states that compatible chemical reaction enthalpies add when their equations add. Reversing a chemical reaction reverses its enthalpy change; multiplying the entire chemical reaction equation by a factor multiplies that change by the same factor. The reason is that enthalpy is a state function: intermediate states cancel from the differences. A cycle supplies one independent balance relation; it cannot determine two unknown inputs without further information.
The law is named after Germain Henri Hess.
For specified initial and final thermodynamic states, the change is ΔH=Hfinal​−Hinitial​. Because enthalpy is an extensive variable, a quoted reaction ΔH belongs to the amount of substance specified for each species in its chemical equation. Reversing the equation changes the sign; scaling every coefficient scales ΔH; adding compatible equations adds their ΔH values. A per-mole value must say which chemical equation and normalization it uses. Match temperature, pressure, thermodynamic phases, chemical solution compositions and reference states before cancellation; the same formula in a gas and a liquid represents different states.[ref]
The value of Hess's law is that an inaccessible reaction enthalpy can be obtained from measurable transformations. The algebra does not require those transformations to be steps of the actual reaction mechanism. Neither an activation energy nor a reaction rate follows from the endpoint difference: a catalyst may change the reaction rate while preserving the compatible initial and final enthalpies.

Enthalpy cycle (∑cycle​ΔH=0)

Words: 204
Hess's law OurBigBook.com
An enthalpy cycle is a collection of compatible thermodynamic processes that returns the entire material inventory to its initial thermodynamic state. Its signed enthalpy changes sum to zero. This supplies a consistency check and lets a missing change be recovered from the others.
Consider three abstract thermodynamic states A,B,C of the same conserved material inventory at common temperature and pressure. Choose their molar enthalpies, on the same one-mole basis, as
hA​=0,hB​=18kJmol−1,hC​=−7kJmol−1.
(19)
These are constructed values, not material measurements. Endpoint subtraction gives
ΔhAB​ΔhBC​ΔhAC​​=hB​−hA​=+18kJmol−1,=hC​−hB​=−25kJmol−1,=hC​−hA​=−7kJmol−1.​
(20)
Thus +18−25=−7: the two-step route and the direct route have the same molar enthalpy change. Closing the route with C→A gives +18−25+7=0. Shifting every h by the same arbitrary reference constant leaves all these differences unchanged.
The short proof is cancellation:
(HB​−HA​)+(HC​−HB​)=HC​−HA​.
(21)
Adding any finite number of consecutive endpoint differences works the same way. For a closed enthalpy cycle the final HA​ cancels the initial HA​. A nonzero experimental residual can therefore expose mismatched states or measurement error; it does not identify which individual input is responsible.

Hess's law equation cancellation

Words: 166
Hess's law OurBigBook.com
Keep the stoichiometry attached to the enthalpy. Use the same abstract A,B,C and suppose each of two entries fixes an amount of substance for every species:
R1​:R2​:​2A⟶2B,C⟶B,​​ΔH1​=+36kJ,ΔH2​=+25kJ.​
(22)
Here each unit coefficient represents one mole on the common basis. To obtain A→C, halve R1​ and reverse R2​. Adding those transformed chemical equations gives
21​R1​:−R2​:sum:​A⟶B,B⟶C,A+B⟶B+C,​​21​ΔH1​=+18kJ,−ΔH2​=−25kJ,ΔH=−7kJ.​
(23)
The equal amounts of B on opposite sides cancel, leaving A→C. Doubling this final chemical equation would give 2A→2C and ΔH=−14kJ; its change per mole of A would remain −7kJmol−1.
More generally, write each chemical equation as a stoichiometric vector νj​, with negative entries for reactants and positive entries for reaction products. Finding coefficients aj​ with νtarget​=∑j​aj​νj​ also gives ΔHtarget​=∑j​aj​ΔHj​, using compatible state and amount conventions. An identical chemical species cancels only with the same thermodynamic phase and composition conditions. A leftover water or dilution step is a real part of the balance.

Hess's law calorimetry experiment

Words: 513
Hess's law OurBigBook.com
A practical test compares three transformations involving sodium hydroxide: dissolution of the solid, neutralization of its chemical solution by hydrochloric acid, and reaction of the solid directly with hydrochloric acid. In the ideal compatible-state notation, the hydrogen ion and hydroxide give
D:N:D+N:​NaOH(s)⟶Na+(aq)+OH−(aq),H+(aq)+OH−(aq)⟶H2​O(l),NaOH(s)+H+(aq)⟶Na+(aq)+H2​O(l).​
(24)
The hydroxide cancels, whereas the newly formed water remains. Sodium and chloride spectator ions must still be included in the full material inventory when matching actual chemical solutions.
The teaching protocol Calorimetry: Heat of Neutralization Reaction & Hess's Law, Procedure A–C, uses nested insulated cups, a cardboard lid and a thermometer. It mixes 75mL each of 2.0molL−1 hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide chemical solutions; separately it adds 6.00g solid sodium hydroxide to diluted hydrochloric acid, or to 150mL water. It records initial temperatures, stirs, reads temperature every 30s, repeats runs, and extrapolates cooling trends to mixing time. Rapid weighing limits moisture uptake. The Introduction neglects vessel heat capacity and room losses; these are approximations, not a measured calibration. The readout tests whether the inferred enthalpies add, rather than directly measuring a state function.[ref]
Matching the chemical equations alone is insufficient. The direct-acid recipe uses 0.160mol hydrochloric acid, whereas the solution-mixing recipe uses 0.150mol. The dissolution run also does not automatically reproduce the water inventory of the mixed-solution run. Exact closure requires matching initial and final chemical solution compositions and adding any necessary mixing or dilution enthalpies. Agreement after approximate corrections is a limited test, rather than proof of exact cancellation for those recipes.
To improve the calorimetry, use calorimeter calibration for the participating hardware, and estimate calorimeter heat-loss correction under comparable conditions. With an approximately constant total receiving heat capacity Ctot​=mcp​+Ccal​, common initial temperature, constant external pressure, only expansion work, negligible escaping material and negligible bulk kinetic energy and potential energy changes, the balance is
qrxn​+Ctot​ΔT+Qloss,out​=0,ΔHrxn​=qrxn​.
(25)
Here m is the chemical solution mass, cp​ its specific heat capacity at constant pressure, Ccal​ the hardware heat capacity, and Qloss,out​ the signed outward heat loss. Different initial temperatures require separate warming terms. Calorimeter calibration and matching chemical solution compositions address different errors.
For an original constructed model, choose Ctot​=120JK−1 and ΔT=3K. Neglect outward heat loss and other corrections. The receiving chemical solution and hardware gain qreceiver​=360J, so qrxn​=−360J. If the completed extent of reaction is ξ=0.020mol for a unit-coefficient chemical equation, the inferred reaction enthalpy per mole of that reaction is
ξΔHrxn​​=0.020mol−360J​=−18kJmol−1.
(26)
These chosen numbers illustrate the signs and normalization; they are not measured sodium hydroxide data and are independent of the abstract A,B,C example.
A loss of heat to the room makes the uncorrected warming underestimate the magnitude of a heat-releasing reaction. Incomplete dissolution, incomplete reaction, uncertain amount of substance, or a slow thermometer response can also spoil closure. A useful experimental residual is r=ΔHdirect​−(ΔHD​+ΔHN​) after all changes have been placed on the same amount and state basis. Compare r with the measurement uncertainty, accounting for shared calibration errors; averaging repeated runs reduces scatter without removing a common bias.

Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔHf∘​)

Words: 43
Thermochemistry OurBigBook.com
The standard enthalpy of formation is the enthalpy change for forming one mole of a specified chemical substance from its chemical elements in their reference states at the stated temperature. For sodium chloride at 298.15K, those reactant states are solid sodium and diatomic gaseous chlorine. Standard state specifies conditions; it does not by itself select a temperature.

Enthalpy of atomization (ΔHat∘​)

Words: 37
Thermochemistry OurBigBook.com
An enthalpy of atomization is the enthalpy change for making one mole of separated gaseous chemical atoms from a specified starting chemical substance. For sodium, the relevant step is sublimation to monatomic gas; for diatomic chlorine, it is half the compatible molar bond-dissociation energy expressed as an enthalpy.

Enthalpy change of solution (ΔHsol​)

Words: 25
Thermochemistry OurBigBook.com
An enthalpy of solution is an enthalpy difference for dissolution into a specified solvent at stated temperature and final concentration. Keep a measured finite-dilution value distinct from an infinite-dilution reference value.

Mass spectrometry

Words: 2k Articles: 19
Chemistry OurBigBook.com
Mass spectrometry separates and detects ions according to mass-to-charge ratio. It can distinguish isotopes which belong to the same chemical element but have different atomic masses. The instrument measures ions: interpreting the result as a neutral atomic mass requires accounting for electron removal and its ionization energy. For a singly positive ion in its ground state, m+​=ma​−me​+I/c2, where me​ is the electron rest mass, I is the ionization energy, and c is the speed of light.
For a simple illustrative analyzer, positive ions of mass m and electric charge q=ze gain kinetic energy qV=mv2/2 across an electric potential difference V before entering a transverse uniform magnetic field B. The Lorentz force supplies centripetal acceleration, so
qvB=rmv2​,qm​=2VB2r2​.
(27)
At fixed V and B, the measured bending radius r separates mass-to-charge ratios, not masses independently of electric charge. This ideal model assumes negligible initial kinetic energy and speeds small compared with the speed of light; the historical focusing mass spectrograph used the geometry described below.
The experimental achievement is to turn invisible differences between individual ions into separated, calibrated positions. Aston velocity focusing explains how an early mass spectrograph sharpened its images; the velocity-selected magnetic mass analyzer provides an independent model whose equations can be checked directly. The magnesium isotope mass spectrum shows why position, width, and intensity carry different information.

Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry

Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com

Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry

Words: 30
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
A combined analytical method separating compounds chromatographically before mass-spectrometric characterization. Peptide identification in a gel region can suggest a protein identity, but comigration requires independent validation of an assigned band.

Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry

Words: 33
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry follows exchange of exchangeable hydrogen with deuterium and measures mass changes, often after digestion into peptides. Protection can reflect hydrogen bonds, burial or restricted structural opening; altered exchange is not uniquely diagnostic of a binding interface.

Chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry

Words: 30
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry identifies residue pairs joined by a chemical reagent and uses them as spatial constraints on protein structures or assemblies. A distance limit depends on linker chemistry, reactive residue positions and accessible conformations.

Co-fractionation mass spectrometry

Words: 23
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
co-fractionation mass spectrometry quantifies proteins across fractions from a native separation. Similar elution profiles suggest shared assemblies; coincident migration and assemblies that exchange partners are alternative explanations.

Native mass spectrometry

Words: 34
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
native mass spectrometry transfers intact biomolecular assemblies into the gas phase under conditions intended to preserve noncovalent association sufficiently for mass analysis. Charge-state assignment and possible loss of subunits or bound lipids must be considered when inferring stoichiometry.

Tandem mass spectrometry

Words: 47 Articles: 2
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
tandem mass spectrometry selects precursor ions, fragments them, and measures the fragments to constrain precursor identity or structure. In proteomics, fragmentation of peptides provides sequence evidence that can be matched against a database.

Electron capture dissociation

Tandem mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com

Electron transfer dissociation

Words: 18
Tandem mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
Fragmentation of molecular ions induced through electron transfer, useful for preserving and localizing some labile modifications in protein analysis.

Accelerator mass spectrometry

Words: 26
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
Accelerator mass spectrometry uses ion acceleration and particle identification to count rare isotopes relative to abundant ones. For radiocarbon dating, it measures carbon-14 directly rather than waiting to count its beta decays.

Molecular ion

Words: 123 Articles: 1
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
In the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) mass spectrometry convention, a molecular ion is formed by removing or adding one or more electrons to a molecule without fragmentation of its molecular structure.[ref] For example, removing one electron from intact water gives H2​O∙+: two hydrogen and one oxygen chemical atom, total electric charge +e, and an unpaired electron, hence a radical cation. Atom inventory, net electric charge, and electronic state are separate pieces of information. Hydronium, H3​O+, has a different inventory; it is a polyatomic ion, rather than the molecular ion obtained by electron removal from water.

Trihydrogen cation (H3+​)

Words: 29
Molecular ion OurBigBook.com
The H3+ ion. Two electrons occupy a fully bonding three-centre orbital at a triangular geometry; the filled nondegenerate shell differs from the open degenerate shell of neutral ground-state H3.

Mass spectrograph

Words: 548 Articles: 1
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
A mass spectrometry instrument with a photographic readout. In the 1919 apparatus described in Chapter V: The Mass-Spectrograph, a gas discharge produced positive ions. Two narrow slits formed a ribbon beam in a vacuum; plates applied an electric field to spread it, an aperture selected part of it, and a magnetic field bent it oppositely. Focusing reduced the spread caused by differing ion speeds, concentrating a given mass-to-charge ratio into a line on a photographic plate.
The observed quantity was line displacement from a fiducial spot. Known reference lines calibrated displacement against mass-to-charge ratio; repeated exposures with changed magnetic field tested the calibration. Evacuation limited collisions. Comparing line shapes with narrow and wide apertures helped distinguish geometric broadening from photographic spreading. Finite slit widths, plate response, and overlapping molecular or multiply charged ions limited interpretation. See Chapter V: The Mass-Spectrograph (§§33–40: apparatus and photographic procedure; §§43 and 45–46: calibration, aperture comparisons, and accuracy).
In Mass spectra and isotopes by Francis William Aston (Nobel lecture, 12 December 1922), the reported neon lines at 20 and 22 have companions at 10 and 11 from doubly charged ions. That paired pattern and comparison with reference lines support different atomic masses within one chemical element, rather than an atomic mass concentrated at the bulk average. The lecture also describes an earlier failed separation by distillation and partial separation by diffusion, showing why the focused mass spectrum supplied stronger evidence. These numbers used a historical oxygen-based reference scale. The lecture's whole-number rule was an empirical approximation at its stated accuracy, not the modern exact definition A=Z+N.[ref]

Aston velocity focusing

Words: 304
Mass spectrograph OurBigBook.com
In Mass spectra and isotopes by Francis William Aston, printed pp. 10–12, Fig. 1, Francis William Aston describes successive electric and magnetic deflections in one plane, with opposite senses. This geometry focuses a range of ion speeds; it does not require the straight-through cancellation of a velocity selector.
The reason compensation is possible follows from the Lorentz force. In a short region of length ℓE​, a small electric deflection angle has magnitude θE​≃qEℓE​/(mv2): the transverse acceleration acts for a time ℓE​/v, and the deflection angle is the acquired transverse velocity divided by v. A short magnetic region of length ℓB​ gives θB​≃qBℓB​/(mv), since the magnetic force already contains one factor of speed. Slower ions therefore receive a disproportionately larger electric deflection.
An original local approximation makes the focusing idea explicit. At fixed mass-to-charge ratio, replace each region by a small angular kick and include the drift distances in two positive constants a and b. With t=v/v0​, write the detector coordinate as
X(t)=t2a​−tb​,dtdX​​t=1​=−2a+b.
(28)
Choosing the geometry and fields so that b=2a eliminates the first-order speed sensitivity. Indeed,
X(t)−X(1)=at2(t−1)2​.
(29)
A fractional speed error ε=t−1 then contributes only at order ε2 in this approximation. This is a local thin-kick explanation, not Aston's exact pole geometry, focal-plane equation, or a prediction of its measured mass resolution. Finite slit widths, initial directions, and field boundaries still matter. Unlike a velocity selector, focusing can collect nearby speeds into a narrow image instead of discarding all but a narrow accepted range.

Velocity-selected magnetic mass analyzer

Words: 192
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
Reuse the velocity selector analysis in the Thomson charge-to-mass experiment, but now send positive ions with q=ze into a separate magnetic analyzer. The selector fields Es​ and Bs​ give v0​=Es​/Bs​. If the analyzer field Ba​ is perpendicular to the selected velocity, its gyroradius gives
qm​=v0​Ba​r​=Es​Ba​Bs​r​,D=2r
(30)
for a semicircular return to the entrance plane. The displayed impact separation D is a diameter. This formula is linear in r at fixed selected speed; the fixed-electric potential difference model above instead gives m/q∝r2. They impose different experimental conditions.
For a chosen example, take Es​=2.00×104V/m, Bs​=0.200T, and Ba​=0.500T. Thus v0​=1.00×105m/s. Approximating an ion mass by 24u and setting q=e gives r≈49.75mm and D≈99.50mm. Here u denotes the unified atomic mass unit. These are stipulated teaching inputs, not a reported Aston measurement or an exact magnesium atomic mass.
A finite accepted speed range broadens the radius distribution. At fixed m/q and Ba​, δr/r=δv/v. At fixed electric charge and mass, K=mv2/2 gives δv/v≃δK/(2K) for a small kinetic energy spread. A one-percent kinetic energy spread therefore produces roughly a half-percent radius spread before other broadening is included. Its width convention must be specified before converting that statement into a mass resolving power.

Magnesium isotope mass spectrum

Words: 419
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
For a modern chosen example, the National Institute of Standards and Technology lists neutral magnesium atomic masses 23.985041697u, 24.985836976u, and 25.982592968u, with reference isotopic abundances 0.7899, 0.1000, and 0.1101. They describe the isotopes with mass numbers 24, 25, and 26, respectively.[ref] These modern inputs are not a reconstruction of historical observations.
Use the dimensionless mass-to-charge ratio coordinate x=(m/u)/z. For the illustration only, approximate ion masses by the neutral atomic masses. The singly charged positions are then near 23.98504, 24.98584, and 25.98259; the doubly charged companions are near 11.99252, 12.49292, and 12.99130. The neutral-to-ion correction already given above is essential at higher accuracy. A peak near x=12 alone need not identify a chemical element: another ion with a different electric charge can occupy the same mass-to-charge ratio interval.
For the narrow singly charged peak at x≈24.98584, the chosen full width at half maximum Δx=0.12 gives mass resolving power R≈208.2; widening to Δx=1.20 gives R≈20.82. Adjacent isotope spacings here are approximately one unit in x. Peaks are visibly separated in the first chosen profile and overlap strongly in the second. A small uncertainty in a fitted peak centre would not by itself make the overlapping components resolved.
Even integrated peak areas need a response model. For isotope fraction fi​, let ηi,z​ collect the probability of ionization into electric charge state z, transmission through the analyzer, and the detection response. In a linear instrument with overall exposure factor C, the component area is
Ai,z​=Cfi​ηi,z​.
(31)
Equal ηi,z​ at a fixed z makes normalized areas equal the fractions; otherwise it does not. In the chosen example, doubling only the mass-25 response changes the normalized areas to 0.71809, 0.18182, and 0.10009, although the neutral sample is unchanged. Photographic darkening introduces another possible nonlinearity: neither line darkness nor peak height is a universal measure of neutral isotopic abundance. Calibration of position and calibration of intensity answer different questions. Matched standards, a known electric charge assignment, and a response correction make isotope analysis useful; a visually impressive set of peaks alone does not supply those controls.

Mass-to-charge ratio (m/q)

Words: 50
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
The ratio of an ion's mass to its electric charge; in SI it has units kg/C. A convenient numerical mass spectrum coordinate is x=(m/u)/z, with q=ze and positive integer z here. This x is dimensionless. Doubling z at fixed mass halves x, so the electric charge state must be identified before assigning an isotope.

Mass spectrum

Words: 156
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
A mass spectrum displays detected signal against mass-to-charge ratio. Peak positions identify candidate ions; peak areas give isotopic abundances only after the response and overlapping contributions have been accounted for.
Broadening can hide a weak component without changing its area in this ideal model. An actual mass spectrum can also contain molecular ions, different electric charge states, background, and unequal detection responses. A missing visible peak therefore cannot by itself prove the absence of an isotope. Conversely, a fractional atomic weight is a property of a population: there is no requirement for an ion peak at the weighted mean.

Mass resolution (R=x/Δx)

Words: 79
Mass spectrometry OurBigBook.com
Mass resolving power compares a peak coordinate x with a stated width or separation criterion Δx. With Δx taken as full width at half maximum, a Gaussian function of standard deviation σ has
Δx=22log2​σ,R=Δxx​.
(32)
At the neon-20 coordinate in the synthetic mass spectrum, σ=0.04 gives Δx≈0.0942 and R≈212, while σ=0.70 gives Δx≈1.648 and R≈12.1. The width criterion and relative peak areas both matter when judging whether a small neighboring isotope can be distinguished. Mass resolution also differs from the accuracy of a calibrated peak position.

Jöns Jacob Berzelius

Chemist OurBigBook.com

Distillation

Words: 1k Articles: 12
Chemistry OurBigBook.com
Distillation separates a mixture by producing vapor from a liquid and collecting the condensed liquid, called the distillate. The more volatile component can have a higher mole fraction in the vapor. Simple distillation collects this condensate directly; fractional distillation adds repeated contact in a fractionating column.[ref]
Two questions must be kept separate. Vapor-liquid equilibrium describes which compositions can coexist. A distillation material balance accounts for how much of each component leaves in each product. A product can be enriched without containing all the original component, and even a feasible distillation material balance does not establish that an apparatus can make those products.

Vacuum distillation

Words: 5
Distillation OurBigBook.com
Vacuum distillation carries out distillation at reduced pressure.

Laboratory condenser

Words: 51
Distillation OurBigBook.com
A laboratory condenser removes heat from vapor so that it becomes liquid. In distillation, the downstream laboratory condenser makes collectable distillate. Complete condensation, without loss or reaction, preserves the entering vapor's overall component mole fractions; cooling alone does not give another enrichment step. Partial condensation can instead leave two streams of different composition, requiring both vapor-liquid equilibrium and a distillation material balance.

Simple distillation

Words: 60
Distillation OurBigBook.com
In simple distillation, pot vapor passes directly to the laboratory condenser. An initial small condensate sample can approximate vapor-liquid equilibrium with the current pot liquid. Removing enriched distillate depletes the pot's more volatile component. A collected fraction averages the changing condensate composition, rather than preserving the first-drop mole fraction.[ref]

Fractional distillation

Words: 237 Articles: 3
Distillation OurBigBook.com
Fractional distillation brings rising vapor into contact with descending liquid in a fractionating column. Packing supplies contact area; it does not act as a sieve for individual molecules. Repeated exchange can enrich the rising vapor in the more volatile component. Some condensed liquid returns downward as reflux, rather than all being withdrawn as distillate.[ref]
An equilibrium stage is an idealization of this contact. A real fractionating column has finite contact time and imperfect wetting and mixing; its length is not automatically a count of equilibrium stages. Product withdrawal and reflux affect the separation together. Thus the repeated ideal-stage enrichment example illustrates the composition advantage of repeated equilibration, but supplies neither a column design nor a specified reflux requirement.[ref]

Fractionating column

Words: 33
Fractional distillation OurBigBook.com
A fractionating column provides contact between rising vapor and returning liquid during fractional distillation. Packing or trays provide contact area; the resulting separation depends on both vapor-liquid equilibrium and the actual flow and exchange between the thermodynamic phases.[ref]

Equilibrium stage

Words: 37
Fractional distillation OurBigBook.com
An equilibrium stage models a contact whose outgoing liquid and vapor satisfy vapor-liquid equilibrium at the stage's temperature and pressure. It is a composition model, not a claim that each piece of packing reaches thermodynamic equilibrium.[ref]

Reflux

Words: 44
Fractional distillation OurBigBook.com
Reflux is condensed liquid returned toward the heated part of a distillation apparatus. In a fractionating column, descending reflux contacts rising vapor. Returning more condensate also changes the amount available for collection, so enrichment and product recovery must be considered together.[ref]

Relative volatility (α=x/(1−x)y/(1−y)​)

Words: 311 Articles: 1
Distillation OurBigBook.com
For a two-component mixture, let x be component A's mole fraction in the liquid and y its mole fraction in the coexisting vapor. At interior compositions, define the relative volatility of A with respect to B by the ratio of composition odds:
α=x/(1−x)y/(1−y)​.
(33)
Thus α>1 means A is enriched in the vapor, while α=1 means y=x. Solving this definition gives
αx(1−y)=y(1−x),y=1+(α−1)xαx​.
(34)
Here a constant relative volatility is a stipulated model of vapor-liquid equilibrium, not a measured property of a named chemical solution. Real relative volatility can vary with composition, temperature, and pressure. The relation specifies no absolute temperature scale: even fixing α=2 does not determine a boiling-temperature curve or a heat requirement.

Repeated ideal-stage enrichment (xn+1​=2xn​/(1+xn​))

Words: 208
Relative volatility OurBigBook.com
Stipulate a constant relative volatility α=2. The vapor-liquid equilibrium model then becomes
y=1+x2x​,y−x=1+xx(1−x)​>0(0<x<1).
(35)
An initial liquid mole fraction x0​=3/10 gives an equilibrium vapor mole fraction y0​=6/13≈0.461538. Now imagine completely condensing a small sample of that vapor and using this condensate as a fresh liquid for another equilibration. Repeating this formal operation gives
x0​=103​=0.300000⟼x1​=136​≈0.461538⟼x2​=1912​≈0.631579⟼x3​=3124​≈0.774194.
(36)
These are original model calculations of ideal-stage enrichment. They are not measured compositions, a reflux design, or successive compositions of one pot undergoing simple distillation. That pot loses the more volatile component and becomes depleted; each step here instead starts from the previous enriched condensate. The displayed sequence specifies compositions, not the recoverable amount at each step.
The algebra makes the enrichment especially transparent. With composition odds rn​=xn​/(1−xn​), every formal step doubles the odds, so
rn​=2n73​,xn​=7+32n32n​.
(37)
For every finite n, xn​<1, although xn​→1 as n→∞. This explains why repeated ideal equilibration can improve composition without making finite-step perfect separation a consequence of the model.

Distillation material balance (F=D+B,Fz=DxD​+BxB​)

Words: 168
Distillation OurBigBook.com
Consider a nonreacting two-component mixture processed into just two products, with no losses or unaccounted inventory. Let F,D,B be feed, distillate, and bottoms amount of substance values in moles, and let z,xD​,xB​ be their component-A mole fractions. These are whole-stream compositions; xD​ is not automatically the instantaneous equilibrium vapor composition y above the pot. Total and component balances give
F=D+B,Fz=DxD​+BxB​.
(38)
The component-B balance follows by subtracting the second equation from the first. Eliminating B gives, for xD​=xB​,
FD​=xD​−xB​z−xB​​,FB​=xD​−xB​xD​−z​.
(39)
Nonnegative product amounts require z between xB​ and xD​. For an original stipulated feed F=1mol, z=0.35, xD​=0.80, and xB​=0.10,
D=145​mol,B=149​mol.
(40)
Check the component inventories:
DxD​=72​mol,BxB​=1409​mol,72​+1409​=207​=0.35.
(41)
The distillate contains a fraction (DxD​)/(Fz)=40/49≈0.816327 of the original component A, despite its higher mole fraction xD​=0.80. This distinction between composition and recovery is useful when deciding how much enriched product to collect. These balances determine neither temperatures, heat input, nor the number of equilibrium stages; they do not prove that the specified products are attainable in a particular fractionating column.

Paired simple and fractional distillation experiment

Words: 172
Distillation OurBigBook.com
McMaster University's 1997/98 laboratory manual compares simple distillation and fractional distillation using charges of 25mL each of cyclohexane and p-xylene. Part B uses a 100mL round-bottom flask and a fractionating column. The protocol specifies a boiling chip, a heating mantle on a ring support, and the top of the thermometer bulb midway in the opening toward the laboratory condenser. Heating is adjusted for roughly one drop per second. Students record head temperature every 2mL collected, up to 45mL, and plot both runs against collected volume on the same axes.[ref]
Charge, atmospheric operation, and collection rate provide comparison conditions; the fractionating column is changed. A sharper separation of temperature regions would support improved fractionation. It would not directly measure product mole fractions or prove purity. The manual distinguishes collected volume from composition and states that this pair forms no azeotrope. No student dataset is supplied here, and the constant-relative volatility example is not assigned to these liquids.[ref]

Azeotrope

Words: 68
Distillation OurBigBook.com
An azeotrope has equal coexisting liquid and vapor compositions: y=x. Ordinary fractional distillation cannot cross this composition boundary at fixed pressure; more packing does not remove it. A constant head temperature therefore does not establish a pure chemical substance.[ref] The stipulated α=2 model has y>x throughout 0<x<1, so it has no interior azeotrope and cannot represent this limit.
